articleTitle: Corn Plants Disease Detection and Prediction using Deep Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Agriculture plays an important role in a country, and agriculture also contributes greatly to the survival of mankind. It is important to obtain pesticide-cleaning crops to improve yields in agriculture. If there are pest-rich crops, it produces good yields and increases the country’s income. The research is now based on IT-based technologies to detect infectious diseases in crops. To do so, an ensemble model is tested. The Ensemble model combines three deep learning model with EfficientDet, Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN) and Single-Shot-Detector (SSD). Research combines three deep learning models and ensemble models to detect and estimate diseases that fall in corn leaf using images of corn obtained from the Plant Village data set. Using the Ensemble Model, the proposed system will select the bounding box detected by the three models. And then, the system will select the suitable bounding box using Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS). Therefore, testing with an ensemble model that combines three models provides a more accurate result than searching for and predicting microbes that can fall in corn using each Deep learning model. With the Ensemble model, more than ten thousand training images and more than three thousand testing images, mAP Score receives 95.00. The result is acceptable in finding and estimating insects that fall in plants.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Real Time Temperature and Humidity Monitoring and Data Logging System Using ESP32
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to monitor the weather in Mandalay, where temperatures are high, in order to protect children and the elderly from heatstroke. In this research, the weather is monitoring and data logging using TTGO Call ESP 32 with Wi-Fi module, DHT 11 temperature and humidity sensor, 16*2 LCD display with I2C interface. Real Time Clock RTC is used for real time applications. The 16*2 LCD display is used to easily view weather data. The http protocol data logging system is used in this research. The weather data has been data logging to the server by using PythonAnywhere cloud-based platform to view from any location. The temperature and humidity data of the first six months of 2024 were obtained from the PythonAnywhere server, downloaded as a CSV file and analyzed and compared using charts.

Author Keywords: TTGO Call ESP 32 with Wi-Fi Module

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of YARA and VirusTotal Integrations with Wazuh for Enhanced Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: For modern cybersecurity defenses, efficient malware detection and response are essential. This paper examines and compares the integration of YARA and VirusTotal with Wazuh, an open-source security information and event management (SIEM) platform with a focus on their ability to identify malware using the EICAR test file, a standardized test sample used to assess antivirus results. The configuration processes for both integrations are assessed, along with their overall effects on detection accuracy, response time and resource usage as well as how well they detect the EICAR test file. According to evaluation results, VirusTotal and YARA gain same results in terms of detection accuracy when it comes to detecting known malware. For response time, YARA’s local processing capabilities outperform VirusTotal significantly as the number of samples increases. For resource usage, YARA uses less memory and CPU because of its local processing, while VirusTotal uses more resources because of its multi-engine scanning method.

articleTitle: ColorRefineNet: Color Refining Underwater Image Enhancement based on Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: In recent times, the challenges associated with underwater images have gained more attention, particularly in color enhancement, which are significant obstacles for high-level computer vision tasks. To solve these issues, this paper proposes a color refinement network, named ColorRefineNet, which is designed to enhance the brightness of color and contrast of underwater images while preserving structure details, sharpness, and colorfulness. In ColorRefineNet, a channel and spatial attention-based Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) attention module is incorporated into each ConvBlock of the baseline Shollow-UWnet. Additionally, a structural similarity (SSIM) loss function is integrated as an additional loss to enhance the color and contrast of underwater images. Comprehensive experiments on eight underwater image datasets, such as EUVP-Dark, UIEB, UFO-120, U45, C60, T90, ColorChecker, and OceanDark, show that ColorRefineNet outperforms UCIQE scores than the baseline Shallow-UWnet and state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.

articleTitle: Improving Brain Cancer Detection and Classification Using Xception Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The detection and classification of brain cancer needed to do digitized after the rapid growth in the incidence of these kinds of diseases. Various brain tumor classifications are an ongoing research topic made possible by the diversity of cancer features. Local brain images testing in the latest brain images datasets BRAT can be challenging due to their processing time, lower accuracy, and the possibility of overfitting and underfitting. In this paper, Xception Deep Convolution Neural Network (DCNN) model was implemented to test the local images or real images and apply three datasets in this model, analysis the individual result and improve the training speed and stability of neural networks by activations of each layer. The Xception model can significantly reduce the number of parameters and computational complexity without compromising the model’s accuracy. Moreover, this system used popular benchmark datasets such as Kaggle and BRATS, the suggested research Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) image datasets were assessed, and the local validation dataset was proposed. In this research work, this model was achieved the best performance decisions with training accuracy and loss 99±0.005%, validation accuracy and loss 98±0.2%. The main objectives are improving the accuracy of classification, avoiding overestimation along with underestimating, and decreasing down on processing time.

articleTitle: Microservices vs Monolith: A Comparative Analysis and Problem-Solving Approach in Web Development Area
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: With the rising complexity and advancement of web applications, many companies require an architecture that can adapt to their business requirements. This research highlights the pros, cons and appropriateness of monolithic, versus microservice architectures across various application types. Numerous studies suggest that microservice architecture offers benefits in scalability and maintenance compared to systems. The potential of microservices as a solution is explored in this study. An ecommerce web application case study employing microservice architecture is implemented to showcase the advantages of this approach. The aim of this paper is to demonstrate the advantages of utilizing microservices to address the limitations of monolithic systems by presenting a practical scenario using microservices. Overall, this paper provides an in-depth comparison between monolithic and microservices offering insights for stakeholders and developers making decisions, on web development project structures.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Performance of the ECLAT Algorithm using K-means Clustering for Frequently Itemset Mining for Large Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Data mining is an approach to identify the key pattern in Frequent Itemset Mining (FIM) and to find from historical data into very useful data. ECLAT is an aspect of association rule that is applied to determine the relationship connection in item supports. By intersecting the transaction id sets according to the corresponding k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> item sets based on depth-first search, ECLAT algorithm computes the support items. During searching best-selling products, ECLAT requires a lot of memory and processing time for large dataset because of the amount of transaction id sets. By merging the K-means clustering algorithm and ECLAT algorithm, the proposed method aims to determine how the K-means clustering algorithm enhances the performance of ECLAT algorithm to generate support items for large dataset. The retail data items from 100000 to 400000 UK consumers were used to retrieve the support items of the most popular selling goods. Firstly, K-means algorithm grouped the same purchased products to cluster the top selling items and then ECLAT algorithm searches the support items from clustering the famous selling products. According to the experimental results, it can be seen that the silhouette score value in this research is 0.586 to indicate a high-quality cluster, the ideal value of k is 8 clusters between 100,000 and 400,000 data items. ECLAT can search the support items based on the clustering of the top eight selling supplies by setting a minimum support value of 0.00001. The proposed method reduces memory usage and execution time to retrieve the support elements for most popular selling items than the ECLAT algorithm for massive dataset.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Fuzzy Clustering Algorithms for Mapping Sugarcane Ratoon Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Remote sensing is widely used in agriculture to monitor crop health, map harvested areas, and estimate soil properties like moisture, texture, and fertility. High temporal resolution satellite data, combined with fuzzy-based machine learning, enables precise crop mapping. This study focuses on detecting the harvesting period of sugarcane and ratoon crops at the Sugarcane Research Center, Pyinmana, using the Modified Possibilistic C-Mean (MPCM) classifier and the MPCM with Spatial Constraints (MPCM-S) approach. Classifier accuracy was assessed using the Mean Membership Difference (MMD) method. Results show that MMD values ranged from 0.00980 to 0.04117 for MPCM and 0.00196 to 0.03725 for MPCM-S. The highest variance within mapped ratoon fields was 0.000847 for MPCM and 0.0006937 for MPCM-S.

Author Keywords: Modified Possibilistic c-mean Classifier with spatial constraints

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis: Monitoring Apache Kafka with Grafana, JMX Exporter, and Prometheus
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: In the big data era, monitoring and analyzing large amounts of heterogeneous data efficiently has become a major challenge. Monitoring and virtualization tools can significantly influence the performance and behavior of real-time open-source frameworks. The paper provides an analysis of Kafka’s performance by measuring producer and consumer latency and throughput using an integrated monitoring architecture including JMX Exporter, Prometheus, and Grafana. Confirming the experimental results, producer latency can be significantly decreased by up to 30% by increasing the number of partitions, whereas consumer delays may slightly increase because of partition overhead. The throughput investigation indicates that Kafka can achieve balanced producer and consumer throughput by processing a 4.6 MB dataset more effectively with more partitions. The paper offers significant results for improving real-time data processing by demonstrating the scalability and dependability of Kafka's performance when monitored using the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Handling of Out-of-Vocabulary Words in Statistical Machine Translation System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: In machine translation Out of Vocabulary (OOV) word is an issue in low resource languages. OOV refers to those that are not present in the training data or cannot be translated using the corpus. Sometime these words are rare words in training data. Many techniques have been proposed by researchers to alleviate this issue in machine translation. In this paper, to obtain correct translations of target side OOV words by updating corpus for low resource Myanmar-Mon language pairs. The longest common substring method and Jaro Winkler similarity are used to extract the appropriate word for the unknown word from the phrase-based corpus. Mon language is Myanmar dialect and there are different Mon phrases with the same meaning as a Myanmar phrase. Thus, word approximation and phrase table updating are utilized to identify and substitute word to improve translation quality and alleviate OOV problem. Myanmar-Mon machine translation system are trained using phrase-based Statistical Machine Translation (SMT). Improvements are made in terms of word translation accuracy by combining with word approximation method.

articleTitle: Myanmar Spelling Checking and Correction Based On Noisy Channel Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Spelling correction is a crucial task in natural language processing, enabling improved understanding and processing of text by correcting phonetic errors, context errors and typographical errors. This paper uses Noisy Channel Model that provides the probabilistic framework for spelling correction by treating the process of typing as a transmission over a noisy channel, where the intended word is distorted. According to the Bayesian inferences, this model consists of two main components: the language model, which captures the prior probability of word sequences, and the error model, which estimates the probability of spelling errors given the intended word. The data are extracted from UCSY Monolingual Corpus. The Spell-error Corpus is manually created for training the error model. The language model is trained using the Spelling Correction Corpus, which is manually segmented and corrected from the UCSY Monolingual Corpus. Damerau-Levenshtein Distance Algorithm is used for candidates generation. Experimental findings indicate that the spelling correction method effectively addresses each type of error, achieving an overall accuracy exceeding 86% across all error categories.

articleTitle: Neural Sentiment Network Model for Myanmar Language Using Attention Mechanism (AttenSentNet)
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is the process of algorithmically identifying whether the opinion/emotion in social media posts, movie reviews as positive, negative, or neutral classes. It is becoming an important in making decision for business owners because they want to know the feedback of their products. It classifies the sentiment polarities into different classes in the user’s review. This proposed paper aims to predict the sentiment polarity of the user comment review from YouTube channels that are written in Myanmar language by combining BiLSTM (Bidirectional LSTM) and attention mechanism. Although there are many research works of NLP tasks using Myanmar language in machine translation and question answering systems, there are few researches on sentiment analysis tasks. The paper uses the hyperparameter tuning approach that is used to find the optimal parameters in training the neural sentiment model. The AttenSentNet also solves the vanishing gradient problem, which is a long-standing issue in the training the deep learning model. The attention mechanism pays attention to the important sentiment words in the given review. Experiments are tested on the phone product review in Youtube written by Myanmar language. Finally, the experimental results show with the accuracy of AttenSentNet model. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work for sentiment analysis task on Myanmar language using BiLSTM neural network with attention.

articleTitle: Trends and Patterns in Spotify’s Most Played Songs: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the trends and patterns in Spotify’s most-played songs, providing insights into the evolving landscape of music consumption in the digital age. Leveraging extensive data from Spotify, one of the leading music streaming platforms globally, we examine the key factors that contribute to song popularity and analyze how these factors have shifted over time. This research encompasses a wide range of metrics, including total streams, genre distribution, temporal changes, and demographic insights. Furthermore, we compare our findings with traditional music popularity metrics to highlight the unique dynamics of digital streaming. In addition to broad trends, we conduct case studies on select top songs and artists to illustrate the multifaceted nature of musical success in the streaming era. These case studies reveal the complex interplay between social media influence, cultural events, and algorithmic promotion. The findings of this paper have important implications for artists, record labels, and marketers seeking to understand and navigate the rapidly changing music industry. By providing a nuanced understanding of what drives song popularity on Spotify, we aim to contribute to the broader discourse on digital music consumption and its impact on the global music landscape.

articleTitle: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Document Query Automation using Open source LLMs
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Ollama provides access to powerful open-source language models that can be integrated into various applications. It supports local hosting, controlling the model's usage and data privacy. LLMs are large language models also known as deep learning models which are pre-trained on a vast amount of data. Integrating with retrieval augmented generation (RAG) can improve the efficiency of the LLM applications by retrieving custom data. The specific website or input of a particular document file can be integrated into the system. The document queries are automatically added to the Excel file using UiPath Automation. Firstly, the proposed system prompts by directly passing through the two LLM models: the Phi3 model by Microsoft with 3 billion parameters and the Llama 3.1 model by Meta with 8 billion parameters for text input and output, which can be accessed from Ollama released by Meta. To achieve a desired output, the system can also prompt by passing through retrieval augmented generation (RAG). Finally, analyze the results of the two outputs by directly using LLM models and embedding them with RAG. According to the evaluation result, RAG integration with llama3.1 improves response quality and relevance for custom data. Phi3 is better in the latency evaluation result.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of LSTM, Bi-LSTM, and BERT for Automated Essay Scoring
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The rapid progress in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and natural language processing (NLP) has created new possibilities for educational technology, particularly in automated essay scoring (AES). This research explores the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in revolutionizing essay scoring within educational technology. Specifically, it focuses on comparing the effectiveness of three distinct approaches to automated essay scoring (AES): training a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) from scratch, and fine-tuning a pre-trained Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model. Both models are trained and finetuned for each approach using the ASAP dataset from Kaggle’s Learning Agency Lab - Automated Essay Scoring 2.0 competition. Their performance is evaluated based on metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Accuracy. To facilitate practical application, a Python web application built with Streamlit enables users to submit essays, choose a scoring model (LSTM, Bi-LSTM or BERT), and receive feedback based on the selected model’s prediction. This study contributes valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, furthering our understanding of efficient model selection for AES tasks.

articleTitle: A Predictive Analytics Framework for Fraud Detection Using Efficient Resampling Based on Hybrid Ensemble Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Financial fraud has become a significant threat to companies and organizations in recent years. The extent of bank fraud is difficult to ascertain because much of it remains undisclosed or undetected. Despite numerous measures to prevent financial fraud, it continues to negatively affect individuals and businesses, with losses from fraud on the rise. Today, most financial transactions are conducted virtually worldwide, and online fraud incurs multi-billion-dollar losses for the global economy annually. Consequently, fraud detection has become one among the most formidable real-life problems. Imbalanced datasets are part of the main difficulties in fraud detection. Additionally, the constantly changing nature of fraudulent behavior complicates the instructional process for state-of-the-art binary classifiers in machine learning. In this work, an extensive predictive analytics framework is introduced for identifying fraud cases and addressing the issue of Imbalanced datasets in training fraud detection models. This framework is constructed through the experimentation with a combination of sampling algorithms with Hidden Markov Model, feature engineering techniques. The proposed framework offers a data-centric method utilized for financial credit card analysis of Imbalanced data with real time transactions and is adaptable to other fields in all financial transaction types of large datasets.

articleTitle: Implementing Hadoop and Moodle Integrated Student Support System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Learning management systems (LMS) generate large amounts of real-time data which has the potential to provide valuable insights. Hadoop MapReduce is a scalable framework that is designed to handle such data. This paper presents a system architecture that integrates Hadoop MapReduce into Moodle, a popular LMS, for analyzing academic data. The implementation of the architecture allows users to generate a variety of reports from student attendance logs through a Moodle plugin which utilizes the Hadoop cluster for processing data. Users such as lecturers can then utilize these reports to identify which students do and do not engage in which courses as well as monitor their eligibility for exams. The use of Hadoop MapReduce provides high performance computing (HPC) capabilities that offer distributed parallel processing and economical scalability by means of adding commodity nodes to the cluster.

articleTitle: Exploring Extractive and Abstractive Approaches for Myanmar Language Text Summarization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Text summarization is one of the most difficult natural language processing (NLP) tasks. It is the process of creating concise, intelligent summaries from a variety of sources, including books, news articles, and social media posts. This method saves readers time in today's busy environment while giving them fast access to important information. This paper presents extractive and abstractive summarization approaches for Myanmar text. While abstractive summarizing creates the complete summary from scratch using the input text, extractive summarization chooses a subset of sentences from the original text for the summary. Abstractive summarizing is more sophisticated than extractive summarization since it involves human-like elements to create the summary from the ground up. The TextRank algorithm and cosine similarity were used for extractive summarization. The mT-5 model, a transformer-based seq2seq model, was employed to carry out abstractive summarization on the XL-Sum dataset. As a result, the extractive summarization of the proposed system yields 43.14 of the ROUGE-1 score, while the abstractive summarization contributes 36.67 of the ROUGE-1 score.

articleTitle: Diabetes Prediction based on Machine Learning Algorithms: MNB, Random Forest, SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The world's diabetes population is growing, which has concerned the medical community and prompted them to look for new ways to advance their technologies. In an effort to develop intelligent and successful diabetes prediction systems, research into machine learning approaches is still ongoing. The aim of this system is to help healthcare providers identify and effectively diagnose diabetes. The system created a machine model to forecast diabetes by utilizing a number of supervised machine learning approaches. This system explores the application of machine learning algorithms—Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—in predicting diabetes using clinical and lifestyle data. The Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases was used to train and evaluate these models. In order to improve the model accuracy, data preprocessing, including feature scaling and handling missing values, was performed. After each algorithm was trained, its performance was assessed using measures including ROC-AUC, F1 score, recall, accuracy, and precision. Random Forest demonstrated high accuracy and robustness, efficiently handling complex interactions among features, while SVM showed strong performance in high-dimensional data settings. Multinomial Naive Bayes, although simpler, provided a baseline for comparison. The results suggest that Random Forest and SVM are effective tools for diabetes prediction, offering a promising approach for early diagnosis and intervention in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Traffic Injury Severity Prediction System using Factor Analysis based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Year to year, due to the road traffic crashes which cost about 3% of the gross domestic product in most of the developed countries is recorded approximately 1.25 million of fatalities. Traffic accidents remain the major causes of death which impose a tremendous economic and emotional burden on society across the world. In the missions to tackle this universal problem, numerous studies have been conducted in an effort to identify the risk factors associated with the injuryseverity level of the crashes. So, this system is intended to explore the correspondence of factors on accident data analysis based on Mutual Information (MI) approach. The selected group of factors is used to predict the injury severity. The most recent single-vehicle crash data is obtained from the Highway Accident Information Management System, Thailand (HAIMST). In this system, mutual information that is information theory approach is used to select the maximum relevant factors for traffic injury severity prediction. By using maximum relevant factors, this system applies the convolutional neural network (CNN) deep learning method to predict the traffic injury severity levels that are no injury, minor, severe and fatal based on group factors.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Commodity Price Forecasting: LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU Comparison with Variable Window Sizes and Activation Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The purchasing power of a significant portion of Myanmar's population is directly impacted by commodity prices, making it critical to maintain price stability. Developing a robust prediction model is one approach to achieve this stability. This research focuses on forecasting the daily prices of salt, oil, and rice from 2007 to 2020. Advanced recurrent neural network models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), are utilized for this purpose. These models learn from observed data over time to predict future values in sequential data. The impact of different window sizes and activation functions on model performance, specifically comparing ReLU and sigmoid activations are investigated. The models are evaluated using key performance metrics: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and R-squared (coefficient of determination). The proposed approach indicates that the GRU model with a sigmoid activation function consistently outperforms the LSTM and BiLSTM models, achieving the lowest RMSE and highest R-squared values, particularly with a window size of 30. While the BiLSTM model demonstrates strong performance with smaller window sizes and sigmoid activation, the LSTM model's performance is less consistent across different configurations. This experiment provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners aiming to enhance commodity price prediction using advanced neural network models.

articleTitle: Bluetooth-Enabled Smart Juicebot Controlled via Mobile App
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The increasing demand for automation in food and beverage industries has led to the development of devices that can efficiently handle tasks such as drink preparation. This paper presents the design and assembly of an Arduino-based automated Juicebot, aimed at automating the beverage-making process. Juicebot is designed to serve a diverse range of juice combinations, offering users the flexibility to choose from different flavors and create custom mixes. The system incorporates components such as stepper motor, ultrasonic sensors, Bluetooth module, and servo motors, which work together to create a seamless, user-friendly experience. Controlled remotely via a mobile application, Juicebot offers not only convenience but also precision, hygiene, and customization. It is a cost-effective solution for small and medium-sized businesses looking to improve efficiency and customer engagement. The paper discusses the hardware and software design, system flow, testing, and potential future improvements to the system.

articleTitle: DLOps: Developing Deep Learning Aided Burmese Rice Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: In nowadays technology areas, a pivotal concern has emerged. It’s was especially concerning architecting Deep Learning enabled Systems (DLS) and sustainability. Most of DLS were failed while release to production. That’s because of uncertainties in data variations, evolutionary requirements, and model inconsistencies. The one suitable solution is Deep Learning Operations (DLOps). It enhances reproducibility and sustainability in building DLS. It still has challenges and are related to environmental impact, technical maintenance, and economic concerns. The self-adaptation helps to address and overcome these challenges. In this paper proposed a sustainable modularized DLOps pipeline thorough the conceptual MAPE-K Framework to solve technical maintenance and economic concerns. The proposed system addresses the uncertainties in data handling and model training then try to proof out efficient utilization from economic concerns point of view. Further, the proposed system is implemented for a Burmese Rice Price Prediction use case to display DLOps pipeline sustainability from technical maintenance point of view.

articleTitle: A Novel Methodology for Deepfake Detection Using MesoNet and GAN-based Deepfake Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: In the past few years, the development of "Deepfake" videos, which are defined by the use of free software tools based on deep learning, has enabled the production of credible face exchanges in videos with minimum evidence of manipulation. Artificial intelligence-altered videos which have gained widespread attention are known as "Deepfake" videos. They are employed to highly realistically manipulate content (audio, video, and image) to create an appearance that a person said or did something they never actually did. The purpose of these deepfake videos is to spread disinformation about people, including governments and personalities, through the use of deep learning algorithms. These films have been intentionally made global with the aim of frightening people, spreading misinformation and marketing, and disrupting society. Deepfake technology uses algorithms like Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to produce artificial images or videos that look realistic. In GANs, a generator and discriminator collaborate to produce phony images or videos that have an authentic look. DeepFaceLab is a free tool for creating deepfakes with a lot of generating flexibility. A deepfake video is quite hard for an average viewer to identify. In order to improve the performance of deepfake detection, we proposed a novel MesoNet approach in this research study that can effectively identify photographs as real or fake. The results of the experiment showed that the enhanced classifier (Meso) network model performed about 90% in terms of identifying real from false photographs.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning for Breast Cancer Image Classification Using Pre-trained CNNs and Random Oversampling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The classification of breast cancer images presents significant challenges, especially when dealing with imbalanced datasets that underrepresent minority classes. This study tackles the issue by implementing ensemble learning techniques with pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as ResNet50, GoogleNet, and EfficientNet. The random oversampling method was employed to address the imbalance, which effectively increases the representation of minority classes within the dataset. This study performs detailed data analysis after this adjustment to improve the model’s ability to identify these minority classes. By combining the predictions of the three models into an ensemble, the approach aims to improve both the accuracy and robustness of the classification process. The ensemble method works much better at finding minority classes, as shown by the results of experiments. This proves that it can handle uneven datasets when classifying breast cancer images.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security of WordPress Websites built on Virtual Machine Using Cloud Computing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Virtualization is important in cloud computing and it gained popularity with the founding of VMWare. Storage devices, servers, network resources, and other physical units can all be virtualized with the application of virtualization technologies. This study aims Enhancing Security of WordPress Website built on Virtual Machine using Cloud Computing Technology. Nowadays, WordPress has emerged as one of the most widely used content management systems (CMS) globally. There are various possible risks to be mindful of when managing a WordPress website. This research investigates the integration of cloud computing technology and virtual machines (VMs) in improving the security of WordPress environments, particularly in investigating web-based exploits. By deploying WordPress on a cloud-hosted VM, this study enables an isolated, scalable environment for analyzing vulnerabilities. This system includes the use of several methods such as Virtual Machine Setup in Cloud Environment, Network Traffic Analysis (Cisco Firepower Device), Web Application Security (F5 Device), Penetration Testing Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP) and jmeter, Automated Security Updates (plugins, Themes) and Regular Backup and Recovery (HPE backup server). These methods outline a systematic approach for investigating web exploits and enhancing the security of a WordPress website hosted on a virtual machine. And the findings of this research suggest that cloud-based VMs can serve as a crucial element in future WordPress security frameworks, offering enhanced flexibility, resilience, and investigative capabilities against emerging web exploits.

articleTitle: Transforming Tech Hiring: BERT-Powered Neural Networks for Automated Job Title Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: In the development of the technology era, the ever-expanding job market exposes an intimidating challenge for job seekers to navigate through the opportunities of securing their desired job positions. Hence, it is of utmost importance to precisely identify suitable job titles for job descriptions, skills and qualifications relating to individual candidates during the recruitment process. The proposed methodology aims to classify the job titles within the domain of IT-focused job dataset utilizing Word Piece tokenization following the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) embedding with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for multi classification. The comparative study demonstrates that the proposed approach, combining BERT embedding with CNN, achieves approximately 86% accuracy and F1 score outperforming traditional classification models, neural networks, and BERT-based classification models.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of CNN, LSTM, and Autoencoder Models of IoT Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: With the rise of Internet of Things (IoT) networks, the need for faster, complex and optimized anomaly detection system to protect the network is more important. This research paper offers a comparison between three emerging deep learning algorithms: Autoencoders, LSTM networks, and CNN towards anomaly detection in IoT setting. Using dataset, IoT-23, we demonstrate these techniques using several evaluation metrics such as accuracy, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Precision-Recall Area Under Curve (PR-AUC). CNNs were the top-performing model with the highest PR-AUC, the lowest MAE, and significantly higher accuracy which we set as the new record in the field. When tested and evaluated, LSTMs had better accuracy and PR-AUC as compared to other algorithms such as Autoencoders which were also found to be useful.

articleTitle: Attention-based CNN Model for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: The application of computer vision techniques to image segmentation tasks in remote sensing images has been steadily increasing in importance. This process partitions an image into non-overlapping segments with semantic significance. There are still problems such as insufficient segmentation accuracy, loss of small targets, segmentation gaps, and loss of information. Pixel-level classification can be performed using semantic image segmentation, which allocates a class to every pixel in an image. However, segmenting targets into multiple categories remains a challenge. The proposed system uses Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) with UNet (U-shaped network) to improve the feature extraction capability of convolution layer from input image at downsampling. Downsampling and upsampling networks use self-attention layers that provide an efficient way to capture dependencies in an image. Semantic representation of feature map is reconstructed with self-attention. The feature map is decoded by upsampling to obtain the desired segmentation result. The proposed system uses channel attention in first and third upsampling stages and spatial attention in second, fourth and fifth upsampling stages at different feature fusion to improve performance across categories. Experiments are conducted on WHDLD dataset, and the results show a high IoU score for segmentation such as baresoil, building, road, and water. Mean IoU is 61.27, and 83.81% of accuracy is obtained.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-based Image Enhancement and Ensemble CNN Model for Bone Fracture Detection and Classification System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Bone fracture detection and classification play a critical role in the early diagnosis and treatment of orthopedic conditions. However, medical X-ray images often occur from low contrast and noise, complicating accurate fracture identification. So, this system is proposed as the effective system that integrates fuzzy-based image enhancement techniques with an ensemble Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for bone fracture detection and classification. To enhance image quality and diagnostic performance, this system combines the histogram equalization (HE) enhancement method with a fuzzy logic triangular membership function. This fuzzy-based enhancement method adjusts image contrast dynamically by utilizing fuzzy logic to improve the visibility of bone structures in noisy or low-contrast medical images. In this system, the enhanced images are then fed into an ensemble CNN model, designed to leverage the strengths of ResNet-50 and VGG-16 deep learning methods. To show the high precision in both detecting and classifying different types of fractures, this system is tested by using the MURA (Musculoskeletal Radiographs) dataset. The result shows that the proposed system outperforms the traditional image processing and single-model CNN approach. This system also supports to reduce the workload of medical professionals and minimize diagnostic errors.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Efficacy of ChatGPT in Different Domains: Customer Support vs. Educational Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: ChatGPT performs with striking contrasts regarding customer service and education, lessons learned in why that is the way it is, how the study uses it, and what the study can do to improve this. ChatGPT is excellent for customer support and the response to the common questions it was built on may be fast and accurate. This is to help both users and resolve issues. Each day’s work is treated as quality, however, when demonstrating more troublesome or irregular problems it comes up short. If the study were to improve this cloud function by making it better at handling complex queries and sounding a lot more human, the study chatbot could perform much better in this and many other domains. But it’s usually wrong and users have reported mixed outcomes. This research proposes how challenging it can be to communicate complex concepts and relate to diverse learning styles. This research will improve ChatGPT for support and as an assistant in each context where it is used. The next target of improvement is to solve the lack of contextual helping experience for ChatGPT users. This paper is crucial in informing how the study might cautiously break conversational AI and indeed future engagements with technology beyond dominant use cases and shaped towards inclusive models that stand to have a significantly positive impact on human lives.

articleTitle: Identifying Video Tampering through Optical Flow Analysis: A Focus on Frame Manipulations
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: This research addresses the critical problem of video tampering detection, focusing on frame deletions, insertions, and duplications. An unconventional approach is proposed, utilizing Farneback optical flow to detect inconsistencies in motion patterns indicative of tampering. To enhance the accuracy of optical flow computation, Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) is applied to manage artifacts resulting from compression, lighting changes, and occlusions. Additionally, temporal filtering techniques are employed to reduce noise sensitivity. Our methodology includes evaluating motion consistency across frames, extracting texture features from the flow field, and applying thresholding techniques to identify abnormal motion characteristics. Temporal consistency checks are performed to ensure the persistence of detected forged regions over multiple frames. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving a TPR of 93.15% and a FAR of 6.65%, highlighting its high accuracy and robustness in identifying video tampering.

articleTitle: Custom Object Detection for Fresh and Rotten Fruit Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Automated grading and processing of fruits is a complex task which requires the creation of effective fruit vision detection systems. This paper presents an introduction of Fruit detection and recognition system for grading apples, bananas and oranges though incorporation of deep learning methodologies. For this study, two separate databases of fruits including the Kaggle and Google databases were carefully prepared. The images were annotated with precision and augmented using the Roboflow web-based platform, categorizing each image into one of six classes: fresh apple, rotten apple, fresh orange, rotten orange, fresh banana, rotten banana. After data collection, the next step involved was data partitioning into training and validation datasets through a data splitting technique. Regarding the model training process, the YOLOv8 and YOLOv5 model was used. The evaluation that was conducted on the trained model was impressive, as the system returned a high value for accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and mAP. The proposed system not only can enhance fruit grading efficiency but also has a wide range of applications in other agricultural fields. Moreover, this study helps toward some significant concerns in agricultural industry, particularly in the area of fruit recognition. It aims to improve the automation the automation of post-harvest fruit quality selection, ensuring more efficient and sorting and grading processes. This extensive review is quite beneficial as it provides insights into the future direction on how to better improve automatic fruit picking technology for better efficiency and optimization.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Boosting Algorithms on DDoS Attack Detection with Data Balancing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Today, a lot of people use the Internet of Things (IoT) in organizations, businesses, and daily life. Attackers have taken advantage of this potential for IoT devices to expose the integrity and security of user data. Especially, the security of the internet and user data is seriously threatened by distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. A DDoS attack is a cyberattack, that intends to break down or shut legal traffic from leading to its destination. There are various Machine Learning is employed in this work as classification methods for DDoS attack detection to develop an automated system that can recognize an attack immediately. This research intends a lightweight boosting classification approach to detect DDoS attacks of IoT based on the resampling techniques to minimize the data imbalance. It compares the performance of the proposed approach with AdaBoost, CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM of boosting models based on time, ROC ACU, accuracy, MAE, RMSE, and F1-score. The experimental results demonstrated that the model with 4.079 seconds of the shortest runtime, highest accuracy, and low error rate is XGBoost using the SMOTE technique on the CICDDOS2019 dataset and KDDCUP99 dataset. XGBoost illustrates excellent time efficiency between other models, and it is a pleasant option for scenarios where rapid processing is critical. The accuracy of XGBoost illustrates highest than other models with 0.9998 with Smote and 0.9900 with borderline smote by using CICDDOS2019 dataset as performance. Additionally, it illustrates 0.699 accuracy with smote and 0.9699 of accuracy with borderline smote by using KDDCUP99 dataset. This research proposes an XGBoost classification approach for an effective IoT DDoS attack detection model using SMOTE and borderline SMOTE for balanced resampling.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Ethereum and Polygon for Implementing NFT-Based Certification Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Blockchain technology, when used to authenticate academic credentials, introduces new approaches to dealing with age-old issues like as fraud and inefficiencies. This paper informs readers on the primary roles that education-based enterprises can perform on both Ethereum and Polygon, boosting the possibilities for developing certification systems based on NFTs. Ethereum is popular among developers and has helped to formalize the sector by establishing foundations and adopting standards such as ERC721. Polygon is a Layer 2 scaling technique designed to reduce transaction costs while also improving transaction functionality. The proposed system includes steps around creating NFTs and governing their distribution and lifecycle to ensure genuine tamper proof of academic records with the help of blockchain. This paper will explore the scalability of system and its cost-effectiveness along with simplicity for ease of choosing appropriate blockchain platform for providing secure certificates issuance and verification.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Predicting Hospitalization Time for Diabetes Patients Using Gradient Boosting and Random Forest Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Accurate prediction of hospitalization time for diabetes patients is essential for effective healthcare management and resource allocation. This study employs and compares two advanced machine learning algorithms, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest, comparing the performance after converting categorical variables to numerical values to predict the hospitalization duration using the UCI Diabetes dataset. Both methods were implemented to develop predictive models, and these models were evaluated based on accuracy and predictive power, providing insights into the most effective approach for predicting hospitalization outcomes. For the model evaluations, the common evaluation metrics method will be used. Random Forest achieves a MSE of 5.45, MAE of 1.76, RMSE of 2.33 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.39, whereas Gradient Boosting achieves a MSE of 5.51, MAE of 1.76, RMSE of 2.35 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.38, using the UCI diabetes dataset that include 101766 data and 50 features. The results demonstrate the comparative strengths and limitations of each algorithm, providing insights into their respective predictive capabilities. This analysis aims to inform the selection of the most suitable model for clinical applications, ultimately contributing to enhanced diabetes patient care and optimized hospital resource management.

articleTitle: Attention-Based Neural Networks with TF-IDF Features and BERT Embeddings for Enhanced Course Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: One vital component of the curricula-variable system is course recommendation aiming to identify appropriate courses for students depending on their needs. But when it comes to choosing the best courses, students regularly encounter a cognitive overburden. Predicting the relevance of courses is essential for educational systems. This research enhances text representation for such predictions by integrating TF-IDF features and BERT embeddings. By merging TF-IDF features and BERT embeddings, this research proposes a multi-Head attention mechanism integrated into a feedforward network as a solution to this problem. The effectiveness of the proposed recommendation model is evaluated and compared against a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. It has been found that the proposed model consistently outperforms in terms of ranking quality over a range of recommendation list sizes. NDCG@k, ARHR@k, F1-score, accuracy, precision, recall, and other performance indicators are used to build and evaluate each learning model.

articleTitle: Enhancing Acoustic-based Speech Emotion Recognition Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is a crucial field aiming to enhance machine understanding of human emotions. Among all the variety of data sources, we choose the acoustic features of the speech to explore both positive and negative aspects in feature extraction, aggressive data augmentation, and complex model architecture, highlighting its potential to inflate false confidence (overfitting) and hallucinations if not wielded with caution. Furthermore, our investigation explores the complex link between accuracy and feature set size, highlighting the need to extract rich emotional characteristics from speech. An intriguing finding of our analysis is: downscaling the filter size and learning rate of the neural network works better with small training dataset and the model can differentiate diverse emotions more accurately. This finding paves the way for improving the classification model, potentially leading to more robust emotion recognition systems. This multifaceted analysis goes beyond the conventional focus on accuracy, challenging assumptions and pinpointing areas for future exploration in the ever-evolving field of speech-based emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Analysis of Air Quality Index using Apache Spark Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Air Quality Index (AQI) analysis is crucial for understanding and addressing air pollution problems. This paper emphasizes the importance of AQI analysis, particularly using the Apache Spark framework. The Apache Spark framework is highlighted for its ability to manage large-scale AQI data and perform machine learning tasks using MLlib. This paper describes how to build machine learning pipelines in Apache Spark and apply them to dataset. The overall analysis shows the importance of AQI analysis within the Apache Spark framework and performs the precision of logistic regression and random forest models in predicting and classifying air quality levels and underlines the significance of effective AQI analysis for tackling air pollution and its effects on public health and the environment. After evaluating all models, the classification using the Apache Spark pipeline achieves an accuracy of over 0.96 and a runtime of only 3.54 seconds. The execution times of Logistic Regression (LR) and Random Forest (RF) vary significantly across platforms for Apache Spark pipelines, non-Apache Spark pipelines, and traditional machine learning.

articleTitle: Community Deception Based on Genetic Algorithm Using Graph Local Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Advanced Information Technologies (ICAIT)
abstract: Many researchers have studied community detection attacks in different ways but there is no best method to fool all community detection algorithms. In this study, to concern privacy protection, we aim to generate the perturbation network using genetic algorithm based on heuristic approach from community disclosure by community detection algorithms. Clustering coefficient and randomization of initialization population are applied to ensure the diversity of the solution spaces and to remove the repetition of same chromosomes in population. This system proposes a local features-based mutation approach for generating the adversarial network effective in community deception. The experimental exhibits the optimal strategy with normalizing mutual information (NMI) and Modularity (Q) by running on difference datasets with variety community detection algorithms.
